title: Repository contained no data, no analysis and no site
detail: At commit dab56c9 the repository held a single file, README.md, containing one line (# RentincreaseSF3) with no trailing newline. There was no data, no source list, no documentation and no web content. GitHub Pages was already enabled (legacy build, main branch, root path) but served nothing.
action: Resolved by task T10: the entire site was built from scratch and every value was sourced from an official publisher. Nothing was carried over from the prior state, so there was no legacy data to reconcile.

title: Third-party sites publish a 2026-27 San Francisco allowable increase of 1.7%; the official rate is 1.6%
detail: The SF Rent Board's own Current Rates page and document 571 both state 1.6% for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027 (and 1.4% for 3/1/2025-2/28/2026). At least one widely circulated third-party 'SF rent control calculator' states the current AGA is 1.7% for the same period while also stating the previous period was 1.4% - an internally inconsistent combination, since the official 1.7% belongs to 3/1/2024-2/28/2025. Another third-party guide states the 2025-26 rate was 1.4% and separately that a 90-day notice applies 'for increases of 10% or more', whereas the statute sets the long-notice trigger at greater than 10%.
action: 1.6% adopted throughout. No third-party figure is used anywhere on this site. If any document you hold shows 1.7% for the 2026-27 period, treat it as incorrect.

title: Two sf.gov pages state DIFFERENT banking maturity rules (12 months vs 24 months)
detail: The sf.gov page Banked rent increases states: 'A skipped increase is only banked if at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase. If less than 24 months pass, the skipped increase is lost.' The sf.gov page Learn about rent increases states in its own worked example that a skipped increase failed to bank 'because a full 12 months has not elapsed'. The Banked rent increases page then contradicts itself: its own worked example banks the 1.7% that had been available for only 12 months (moved in 8/1/2022, first increase 8/1/2025, banking both 8/1/2023 at 3.6% and 8/1/2024 at 1.7%).
action: Resolved in favour of the controlling regulation: Rent Board Rules and Regulations Sec. 4.12(a), as published by the Rent Board on sf.gov, reads 'A full 12 months must have elapsed from the date that an annual rent increase, or a portion thereof, could have been imposed before this banking section becomes applicable.' All calculations here use 12 months. The 24-month sentence appears to be an error on that page. Because two official pages disagree, confirm the maturity rule with a Rent Board counselor (415-252-4600) before serving any banked-increase notice. The calculator in this repository reproduces all four official worked examples exactly under the 12-month rule, which is strong corroboration.

title: Rent increase license status is UNKNOWN for both units - no increase is enforceable without it
detail: Under Rent Ordinance Sec. 37.15 and the Rent Board Housing Inventory rules, a current rent increase license must be on file on the EFFECTIVE DATE of the increase or the entire annual or banked increase is null and void, regardless of whether the arithmetic was correct. The license status of these two units was not supplied and is not published anywhere this project can read.
action: Left blank on the unit dossiers - not inferred. Before serving any notice: file or refresh the Housing Inventory at portal.sfrb.org (deadline March 1 each year, late filing is permitted and carries no monetary penalty) and confirm the license covers the effective date. Note the submitted information is PUBLIC and includes base rent in $250 increments.

title: Two sf.gov documents give DIFFERENT operative dates for the Sec. 37.15 licensing requirement
detail: The Housing Inventory page states the requirement became operative July 1, 2022 for non-condo buildings with 10 or more units, with reporting beginning March 1, 2023 for condominiums and buildings with fewer than 10 units. An official Rent Board worksheet PDF (document 538) states the requirement applies to increases effective on or after July 1, 2020 for buildings with ten or more residential units and on or after March 1, 2021 for condominiums and buildings with fewer than ten units.
action: Both dates are published here; neither is used to compute anything, because the license is a present-tense gate that must be satisfied on the effective date of any future increase. Use the more recent Housing Inventory page for current filing obligations and confirm the historical dates with the Rent Board before relying on them in any audit of a past increase.

title: Unit A had a change in occupants - whether a market-rate reset is available turns on facts not supplied
detail: Unit A's original tenancy (began 2025-02-01) had three tenants; the continuing tenancy from 2026-04-01 has two, one of whom is an original tenant and one of whom is new. Two different legal routes could in principle permit a market-rate reset, and both are unavailable on the facts as stated: (i) Cal. Civ. Code Sec. 1954.53(d)(3) expressly does NOT apply 'to partial changes in occupancy... where one or more of the occupants... remains an occupant in lawful possession'; and (ii) Rules & Regs Sec. 6.14 permits an unlimited increase only when the LAST original occupant vacates AND a timely written 6.14 notice was served on each subsequent occupant. Whether the new occupant is a co-tenant (never subject to a Costa-Hawkins reset) or a subtenant, and whether any 6.14 notice was ever served, were not supplied.
action: Analysed on the facts as stated: an original occupant remains, so NO market-rate reset is available and the lawful ceiling stays tied to the $3,995.00 base rent with a February 1 anniversary. The unresolved sub-questions are recorded here rather than assumed. Do not serve a Sec. 6.14 or Costa-Hawkins notice on these facts without a written legal opinion.

title: Base rent composition was not supplied for either unit
detail: The increase must be computed on BASE RENT, which includes housing services such as parking and storage but EXCLUDES temporary passthroughs and fluctuating charges. Whether the $3,995.00 and $3,150.00 figures include parking, storage or any passthrough was not stated.
action: Left blank; the stated figures were used exactly as supplied and no component was inferred. If either figure contains a passthrough, the percentages must be re-applied to the corrected base rent before any notice is served.

title: No record of prior increases, security-deposit interest or Rent Board fee payments was supplied
detail: The calculations assume no increase was ever imposed (Unit A: none since 2025-02-01; Unit B: none since 2019-06-01) because none was reported. Security-deposit interest must be paid annually (4.2% for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027) and the Rent Board fee ($59.00 per dwelling unit for 2026-2027) must be paid by March 1. Compliance with either was not evidenced.
action: Prior-increase history treated as EMPTY and flagged; deposit-interest and fee compliance left blank. A tenant representative will request all three. Assemble the complete rent history and the payment records before serving notice - the Rent Board can order a determination of lawful rent on Form 354 and the burden of proving the correct base rent falls on the owner.

title: The building's construction date is owner-reported, not verified against a public record
detail: Coverage under the Rent Ordinance turns on the building having been built on or before June 13, 1979. 'Built in 1940' was supplied as a statement, not as a document. A 1940 building would be covered, but the project cannot verify the year from the material supplied.
action: Coverage is presented as PRESUMED, not verified. Confirm on the San Francisco Property Information Map and, if needed, obtain a Rent Board determination. Also confirm the unit is not separately alienable (a condominium or single-family dwelling), which would change the analysis under Sec. 1954.52(a)(3) and Sec. 37.3(d)(1)(A).

title: The allowable increase for 3/1/2027-2/28/2028 has not been published
detail: Unit B's recommended scenario takes effect 2027-06-01. The banked total of 13.1% is fully verified, but the annual increase in effect on that date belongs to the period beginning 3/1/2027, which the Rent Board had not published as of 2026-11-06 (it publishes on or about January 1 each year, effective March 1).
action: Left blank everywhere and never forecast. Unit B's total is published as '13.1% + [unpublished]'. Re-run python3 tools/calc.py after the Rent Board publishes the 2027-28 rate and update the AGA table in tools/rentcalc.py.

title: An official Rent Board worked example mislabels which year's rate it is applying
detail: On Learn about rent increases, the example 'RENT INCREASE FOR ONE YEAR ON ANNIVERSARY DATE' says a tenant who moved in 2025-06-01 and is increased on 2026-06-01 gets 'the annual allowable increase in effect on June 1, 2025 is 1.6%'. Per document 571 the rate in effect on 2025-06-01 was 1.4%; the 1.6% rate was in effect on 2026-06-01. The example's RESULT ($1,016.00) is correct if the rate in effect on the EFFECTIVE date is used, which is also what the same page instructs ('use the percentage that will be in effect on the date of the increase').
action: The engine applies the rate in effect on the EFFECTIVE date and reproduces the official result ($1,016.00) exactly. The mislabelled year is recorded here for transparency; it does not change any figure published on this site.

title: The FHFA GSE rent-increase notice requirement could not be confirmed on fhfa.gov
detail: Secondary reporting states that FHFA announced on 2024-07-12 that, for new multifamily loans signed on or after 2025-02-28, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac loan documents would require a 30-day written notice of any rent increase, a 30-day notice of lease expiration and a 5-day grace period for late rent; that implementation was paused to 2025-05-31; and that FHFA then rescinded the directives in March 2025. Neither the announcement nor the rescission could be confirmed: the fhfa.gov newsroom URLs returned 'Page Not Found' on 2026-11-06.
action: The FHFA item is published as UNVERIFIED and is NOT relied on anywhere in the analysis. It is immaterial to these two units, which are governed by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance; it would only matter if the property carried an Enterprise-backed multifamily loan. Confirm the current status directly with FHFA before relying on it.

title: No federal statute sets a rent-increase ceiling for private unsubsidised housing - a negative finding
detail: The federal maximum allowable rent increase is left BLANK. This is a negative finding: the Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. Sec. 3601 et seq.) regulates the MANNER in which rent may be set, not its amount, and federal rent limits attach only to federally assisted housing (for example Section 8 and HUD-insured programmes) or to programme-specific rules. A negative finding cannot be proved by citing a document that states it.
action: Published as 'No federal ceiling - not applicable', with the Fair Housing Act cited for what federal law DOES require. Recorded here so the blank cell is understood as deliberate, not as an omission.

title: All personal information has been removed from the published record
detail: Tenant names, unit designations and any identifying detail were supplied for analysis. Publishing them would defeat the stated privacy requirement, and the Housing Inventory data an owner files with the Rent Board is itself PUBLIC.
action: Unit 1 is published as Unit A and Unit 2 as Unit B. Tenants are published as pseudonymous identifiers (T-A1 to T-A4, T-B1 to T-B2) with the original-to-current mapping shown only as role changes, never as names. All dates and all dollar amounts are preserved EXACTLY as supplied. No street address was supplied and none is published; location is given only as 'San Francisco, CA 94122 (Outer Sunset)'. The mapping between pseudonyms and real identities is held by the owner and appears nowhere in this repository.

title: Sec. 37.8 refund look-back period could not be read from the official compiled ordinance
detail: The compiled Chapter 37 PDF published on sf.gov is long, and only its first pages could be parsed for this project. The table of contents confirms Sec. 37.8 (Arbitration of Rental Increase Adjustments) exists, and Sec. 37.3(b)(5) ('Nonconforming Rent Increases... shall be null and void') was read directly. The specific length of the refund look-back an Administrative Law Judge may order for a null-and-void increase was NOT read from the official text and is therefore not published.
action: The exposure is described qualitatively (a non-conforming increase is null and void and overpayments may be ordered refunded or offset) with no period stated. Obtain the full Sec. 37.8 text before quantifying look-back exposure.

area: Broken link found by the automated check
title: A link to the United States Code returned HTTP 404 and was removed
detail: The source register originally included the Office of the Law Revision Counsel URL for 42 U.S.C. ch. 45 (the Fair Housing Act). The automated link check run in CI returned HTTP 404 for that URL, which was referenced from five pages. A 404 is treated as a dead link and fails the build.
action: The entry was removed and every citation that pointed at it was re-pointed to the U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division page on the Fair Housing Act, which states the statutory citation (42 U.S.C. Sec. 3601 et seq.) itself and returned HTTP 200. No substantive claim was lost: the negative finding that no federal statute sets a rent ceiling for private unsubsidised housing rests on the DOJ and HUD pages, not on the U.S. Code browse URL. The build now passes.

title: Several official hosts refuse automated requests (HTTP 403), so their links cannot be machine-checked
detail: The CI link check received HTTP 403 from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (all seven California code sections and the AB 1482 bill-text page) and from calcivilrights.ca.gov. These hosts block non-browser clients; the pages are live and were retrieved and read directly during research on 2026-11-06. A 403 is therefore recorded as a warning, not as a dead link, and never as verification that content is present.
action: The link checker classifies 404/410 as failures and 401/403/405/429/5xx as warnings, and reports both. The affected sources are marked ‘Verified – retrieved’ in the register on the strength of direct retrieval, not of a status code. Full results are published in docs/verification/link-check.md.
